# sdid: Updated Synthetic Difference-in-Differences Estimation and Inference for R

[![registry status
badge](https://alcocer-jj.r-universe.dev/badges/:registry)](https://alcocer-jj.r-universe.dev/)
[![R-universe](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https://alcocer-jj.r-universe.dev/api/packages/sdid&query=$.Version&label=R-universe&color=blue)](https://alcocer-jj.r-universe.dev/sdid)
[![sdid](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-BSD_3--Clause-orange)](https://alcocer-jj.r-universe.dev/sdid)

This package is intended to help R users estimate average effects on the
treated (ATT) in panel data (under identifying assumptions) using
synthetic difference-in-differences (SDiD). We built this package to
implement key aspects of the related Stata package
[`sdid`](https://github.com/Daniel-Pailanir/sdid) by Clarke et
al. (2024) in R. As in that package, our implementation accepts a long
format panel dataset, detects whether a staggered treatment approach is
needed, and estimates the effect with bootstrap, jackknife, or placebo
inference.

We build on a prior R implementation of this method
[`synthdid`](https://github.com/synth-inference/synthdid) 0.0.9 by
Arkhangelsky et al. (2021), adding staggered adoption, optimized and
projected methods of covariate adjustment, and a redesigned interface.
To substantially reduce computation time, we reimplement the estimation
of the unit and time weights in compiled C++ code and parallelize the
resampling procedures used for inference.

## Installation

The development version can be installed from R-Universe.

\
[`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(``"sdid"``, repos ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"https://alcocer-jj.r-universe.dev"``,`\
`                                   ``"https://cloud.r-project.org"``)``)`

Users who already have a C++ toolchain can also install `sdid` directly
from GitHub, which compiles the package from source.[^1]

\
`# install.packages("remotes")`\
`remotes``::`[`install_github`](https://remotes.r-lib.org/reference/install_github.html)`(``"alcocer-jj/sdid"``)`

## Syntax

A full call of the main function is shown below. For arguments that take
one of several values, the first value listed is the default, except for
`vce`, which has no default and must be given.

\
[`sdid`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid.md)`(`\
`  ``data``,`\
`  ``outcome``,`\
`  ``unit``,`\
`  ``time``,`\
`  ``treatment``,`\
`  vce ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"bootstrap"``, ``"jackknife"``, ``"placebo"``, ``"noinference"``)``,`\
`  covariates ``=`` ``NULL``,`\
`  method ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"sdid"``, ``"sc"``, ``"did"``)``,`\
`  reps ``=`` ``50``,`\
`  seed ``=`` ``NULL``,`\
`  level ``=`` ``95``,`\
`  alternative ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"two.sided"``, ``"greater"``, ``"less"``)``,`\
`  covariate.method ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"optimized"``, ``"projected"``)``,`\
`  standardize ``=`` ``TRUE``,`\
`  projection.sample ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"controls"``, ``"untreated"``)``,`\
`  num.threads ``=`` ``NULL``,`\
`  graph ``=`` ``TRUE``,`\
`  quietly ``=`` ``FALSE``,`\
`  ``...`\
`)`

- `data`: balanced panel in long format, one row per unit and period.
- `outcome`: name of the outcome variable.
- `unit`: name of the unit identifier.
- `time`: name of the time period variable.
- `treatment`: name of the binary treatment variable, equal to 1 for a
  treated unit in every period from its first treated period onward, and
  0 otherwise.
- `vce`: inference method (required).
- `covariates`: names of time-varying covariate variables, if any.
- `method`: synthetic DiD, synthetic control, or
  difference-in-differences.
- `reps`: number of bootstrap or placebo replications.
- `seed`: random seed, applied to this call only.
- `level`: confidence level, in percent.
- `alternative`: alternative hypothesis of the test of the effect
  against zero.
- `covariate.method`: how covariates are adjusted for.
- `standardize`: standardize covariates under the optimized method.
- `projection.sample`: regression sample under the projected method.
- `num.threads`: threads for replications, all available when NULL.
- `graph`: produce the trends plot in this call.
- `quietly`: TRUE prints nothing, for use in loops.

## Example

The example below estimates the effect of California’s Proposition 99 on
cigarette consumption, using placebo inference because California is the
only treated state. An
[`sdid()`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid.md) call
describes the data and parameters in the console, shows the inference
progress, and prints the results.

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`sdid`](https://github.com/alcocer-jj/sdid)`)`\
\
[`data`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/data.html)`(``california_prop99``)`\
\
`fit1`` ``<-`` `[`sdid`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid.md)`(`\
`  ``california_prop99``,`\
`  ``"PacksPerCapita"``, ``"State"``, ``"Year"``, ``"treated"``,`\
`  vce ``=`` ``"placebo"``, reps ``=`` ``1000``, seed ``=`` ``444`\
`)`\
`#> Synthetic Difference-in-Differences Estimator`\
`#> `\
`#> Outcome     PacksPerCapita`\
`#> Treatment   treated`\
`#> Units       39 (38 never treated, 1 treated)`\
`#> Periods     31 (1970 to 2000), treatment from 1989`\
`#> Inference   placebo, 1000 replications`\
`#> `\
`#> Placebo  [========================]  1000/1000  100%  0.2s elapsed  done  18 threads`\
`#> `\
`#>               ATT Std. Err.     z P>|z| [95% Conf. Interval]`\
`#> treated -15.60383   8.71856 -1.79 0.073  -32.69189   1.48424`\
`#> `\
`#> 95% confidence intervals and p-values use the normal approximation.`

It also draws the trends plot unless `graph = FALSE`.

![](reference/figures/plot1.png)

## Staggered adoption

When treated units adopt treatment in different periods,
[`sdid()`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid.md)
estimates adoption-period effects. The overall effect is a weighted
average of these effects with weights proportional to each cohort’s
number of treated units times its number of post-treatment periods,
following Algorithm 1 of Clarke et al. (2024). Bootstrap, jackknife, and
placebo inference then resample the whole panel jointly, as in
Algorithms 2 to 4 of Clarke et al. (2024).

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`haven`](https://haven.tidyverse.org)`)`\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`sdid`](https://github.com/alcocer-jj/sdid)`)`\
\
`data`` ``<-`` `[`read_dta`](https://haven.tidyverse.org/reference/read_dta.html)`(``"https://github.com/Daniel-Pailanir/sdid/raw/refs/heads/main/simulations/cluster_data/quota_example_cluster.dta"``)`\
\
`fit2`` ``<-`` `[`sdid`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid.md)`(`\
`  ``data``,`\
`  ``"womparl"``, ``"country"``, ``"year"``, ``"quota"``,`\
`  vce ``=`` ``"bootstrap"``, reps ``=`` ``1000``, seed ``=`` ``444`\
`)`\
`#> Synthetic Difference-in-Differences Estimator`\
`#> `\
`#> Outcome     womparl`\
`#> Treatment   quota`\
`#> Units       119 (110 never treated, 9 treated)`\
`#> Periods     26 (1990 to 2015), 7 adoption periods`\
`#> Inference   bootstrap, 1000 replications`\
`#> `\
`#> Bootstrap  [========================]  1000/1000  100%  11.4s elapsed  done  18 threads`\
`#> `\
`#>           ATT Std. Err.    z P>|z| [95% Conf. Interval]`\
`#> quota 8.03410   3.18551 2.52 0.012    1.79062  14.27758`\
`#> `\
`#> Adoption-period estimates`\
`#>      Treated Post Weight      ATT Std. Err.     z P>|z| [95% Conf. Interval]`\
`#> 2000       1   16 0.1702  8.38887   0.69893 12.00 0.000    7.01900   9.75874`\
`#> 2002       2   14 0.2979  6.96775   0.57747 12.07 0.000    5.83592   8.09957`\
`#> 2003       2   13 0.2766 13.95226   8.59993  1.62 0.105   -2.90329  30.80781`\
`#> 2005       1   11 0.1170 -3.45054   0.67457 -5.12 0.000   -4.77268  -2.12841`\
`#> 2010       1    6 0.0638  2.74904   0.43366  6.34 0.000    1.89908   3.59899`\
`#> 2012       1    4 0.0426 21.76272   0.86701 25.10 0.000   20.06341  23.46203`\
`#> 2013       1    3 0.0319 -0.82032   0.81086 -1.01 0.312   -2.40958   0.76893`\
`#> `\
`#> 95% confidence intervals and p-values use the normal approximation.        `

![](reference/figures/plot2.png)

## Covariates

Time-varying covariates can be supplied with `covariates`, while
`covariate.method` selects one of the two adjustments. The default,
`"optimized"`, estimates their coefficients jointly with the weights,
following Arkhangelsky et al. (2021), after standardizing each
covariate. The alternative, `"projected"`, estimates them from a two-way
fixed effects regression on the never-treated units, following Kranz
(2022) and Clarke et al. (2024).

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`sdid`](https://github.com/alcocer-jj/sdid)`)`\
\
[`data`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/data.html)`(``CPS``)`\
\
`fit3`` ``<-`` `[`sdid`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid.md)`(`\
`  ``CPS``,`\
`  ``"log_wage"``, ``"state"``, ``"year"``, ``"abort_ban"``,`\
`  vce ``=`` ``"bootstrap"``, reps ``=`` ``1000``, seed ``=`` ``444``,`\
`  covariates ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"hours"``, ``"urate"``)``,`\
`  covariate.method ``=`` ``"projected"``,`\
`  graph ``=`` ``FALSE`\
`)`\
`#> Synthetic Difference-in-Differences Estimator`\
`#> `\
`#> Outcome     log_wage`\
`#> Treatment   abort_ban`\
`#> Units       50 (32 never treated, 18 treated)`\
`#> Periods     40 (1979 to 2018), treatment from 2018`\
`#> Covariates  hours, urate, projected`\
`#> Inference   bootstrap, 1000 replications`\
`#> `\
`#> Bootstrap  [========================]  1000/1000  100%  1.0s elapsed  done  18 threads`\
`#> `\
`#>               ATT Std. Err.    z P>|z| [95% Conf. Interval]`\
`#> abort_ban 0.00261   0.01465 0.18 0.858   -0.02610   0.03132`\
`#> `\
`#> 95% confidence intervals and p-values use the normal approximation.`

## Tables

Results work with [modelsummary](https://modelsummary.com) and other
packages that read results through
[`tidy()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/tidy.html) and
[`glance()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html). Each
model’s effect is named by its treatment column by default, so
`labels = "ATT"` puts the effects of models with different treatment
columns on one row. For a staggered design, `cohorts = TRUE` adds a row
for each adoption period, and `labels` can then name every row.

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`modelsummary`](https://modelsummary.com)`)`\
\
`gm`` ``<-`` `[`data.frame`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/data.frame.html)`(`\
`  raw ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"nobs"``, ``"n.units"``, ``"n.periods"``)``,`\
`  clean ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"Observations"``, ``"Units"``, ``"Periods"``)``,`\
`  fmt ``=`` ``0`\
`)`\
\
[`modelsummary`](https://modelsummary.com/man/modelsummary.html)`(`\
`  models ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``"Prop 99"`` ``=`` ``fit1``, ``"Quota"`` ``=`` ``fit2``, ``"Abortion Ban"`` ``=`` ``fit3``)``,`\
`  labels ``=`` ``"ATT"``,`\
`  gof_map ``=`` ``gm``,`\
`  stars ``=`` ``TRUE``,`\
`  output ``=`` ``"markdown"`\
`)`\
`#> +--------------+----------+---------+--------------+`\
`#> |              | Prop 99  | Quota   | Abortion Ban |`\
`#> +==============+==========+=========+==============+`\
`#> | ATT          | -15.604+ | 8.034*  | 0.003        |`\
`#> +--------------+----------+---------+--------------+`\
`#> |              | (8.719)  | (3.186) | (0.015)      |`\
`#> +--------------+----------+---------+--------------+`\
`#> | Observations | 1209     | 3094    | 2000         |`\
`#> +--------------+----------+---------+--------------+`\
`#> | Units        | 39       | 119     | 50           |`\
`#> +--------------+----------+---------+--------------+`\
`#> | Periods      | 31       | 26      | 40           |`\
`#> +==============+==========+=========+==============+`\
`#> | + p < 0.1, * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p <      |`\
`#> | 0.001                                            |`\
`#> +==============+==========+=========+==============+`\
\
[`modelsummary`](https://modelsummary.com/man/modelsummary.html)`(`\
`  models ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``"Quota"`` ``=`` ``fit2``)``,`\
`  coef_rename ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"quota"`` ``=`` ``"Weighted ATT"``)``,`\
`  cohorts ``=`` ``TRUE``,`\
`  gof_map ``=`` ``gm``,`\
`  stars ``=`` ``TRUE``,`\
`  output ``=`` ``"markdown"`\
`)`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> |              | Quota     |`\
`#> +==============+===========+`\
`#> | Weighted ATT | 8.034*    |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> |              | (3.186)   |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> | 2000         | 8.389***  |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> |              | (0.699)   |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> | 2002         | 6.968***  |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> |              | (0.577)   |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> | 2003         | 13.952    |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> |              | (8.600)   |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> | 2005         | -3.451*** |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> |              | (0.675)   |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> | 2010         | 2.749***  |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> |              | (0.434)   |`\
`#> +--------------+-----------+`\
`#> | 2012         | 21.763*** |`\

## Plots

The plotting functions take the result of
[`sdid()`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid.md) and draw
one panel per adoption cohort for a staggered design.

\
[`sdid_plot`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_plot.md)`(``fit1``)`` ``# trajectories and time weights`\
\
[`sdid_plot`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_plot.md)`(``fit1``, style ``=`` ``"effects"``)`` ``# with a DiD effects diagram`\
\
[`sdid_plot`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_plot.md)`(``fit1``, x.breaks ``=`` `[`seq`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/seq.html)`(``1970``, ``2000``, by ``=`` ``5``)``)``  ``# custom ticks`\
\
[`sdid_units_plot`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_units_plot.md)`(``fit1``)`` ``# unit weights`\
\
[`sdid_units_plot`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_units_plot.md)`(``fit1``, type ``=`` ``"bars"``)`` ``# unit weights with bars instead`\
\
[`sdid_placebo_plot`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_placebo_plot.md)`(``fit1``, placebo.time ``=`` ``1981``)`` ``# in-time placebo plot`

![](reference/figures/plot3.gif)

## Performance

Unit and time weights are estimated in C++, and bootstrap, jackknife,
and placebo replications run in parallel across all available threads.
The option `sdid.num.threads`, or the `num.threads` argument of
[`sdid()`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid.md), limits
the number of threads.

build on their methods and the code they made openly available.

## Plots and placebo tests (require ggplot2)

- [`sdid_plot()`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_plot.md)
  : Plot treated and synthetic control trajectories
- [`sdid_units_plot()`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_units_plot.md)
  : Plots each control unit's weight and its own estimate
- [`sdid_placebo_plot()`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_placebo_plot.md)
  : Plot an estimate with its in-time placebo
- [`sdid_placebo()`](https://alcocer-jj.github.io/sdid/reference/sdid_placebo.md)
  : Computes a placebo variant of our estimator using pre-treatment data
  only
